content.text:
### 1. Requirement summary

**Fact:** The requester asked to create a welcome page named **Hari-Agents**.

This specification defines a **single static welcome/landing page** that presents the Hari-Agents identity when a person opens the workspace in a browser. The page must show a clear page title, a greeting, and simple branding for a personal agent workspace.

**Fact:** The workspace at `C:/Users/Hariprasanth_Baskara/.cursor` has no existing HTML/web application and no `package.json`. An existing `requirements.md` at the repo root is a **separate draft** for application logo identity (`US-LOGO-1`), not a welcome-page specification.

**Fact:** No Jira issue, epic, project key, or Confluence page was provided or created for this request.

---

### 2. Business objective

Give the personal agent workspace a recognizable first screen so a visitor immediately knows they have opened **Hari-Agents**, understands that it is a personal agent workspace, and sees a welcoming branded landing surface.

Success looks like: opening the page in a browser (no login, no API) displays the Hari-Agents title, a greeting, and consistent branding; the browser tab name matches the product name; the page remains usable without a backend.

---

### 3. Scope (In scope / Out of scope)

**In scope**

- One static welcome/landing page named Hari-Agents.
- Visible page heading that identifies the workspace as Hari-Agents.
- A greeting message on first view.
- Simple branding for a personal agent workspace (product name, short supporting line, and a coherent visual treatment).
- Browser document title that identifies Hari-Agents.
- Client-side accessibility basics that can be verified in the browser (semantic heading, readable text, keyboard-visible content).
- Layout that remains readable on a typical desktop viewport and a typical mobile viewport.
- Static assets only (HTML and optional CSS/images served as files).

**Out of scope**

- Authentication, accounts, sessions, or role-based views.
- APIs, databases, backend services, or dynamic content.
- Analytics, telemetry, cookies, or tracking.
- Jira, Confluence, or any Atlassian integration **in the page itself**.
- Multi-page application, routing, navigation to other product screens (unless later authorized as a new requirement).
- Agent execution, chat, command launching, or SDLC orchestration from the page.
- A full brand system, logo design system, or PWA/favicon program (the existing logo draft is related but not this story).
- Hosting, CI/CD, domain, or deployment platform selection (architecture decision).
- A prescribed technology stack (architecture decision).
- Creating or updating Jira issues as part of this analysis.

---

### 4. Actors and systems

| ID | Actor / system | Type | Role |
|----|----------------|------|------|
| A-U1 | Workspace owner (Hari) | Human | Opens the welcome page locally or via a later static host to confirm the workspace identity. |
| A-U2 | Casual visitor | Human | Opens the page and must understand the workspace name and purpose without training. |
| A-U3 | Implementer | Human | Builds and visually verifies the static page against this specification. |
| A-S1 | Web browser | System | Renders the static page and shows the document title in the tab. |
| A-S2 | Static file source | System | Serves or opens the page files (file open or later static hosting). Hosting choice is not a requirement. |
| A-S3 | Cursor SDLC command flow | Adjacent process | Downstream architecture, design, implementation, and test agents may consume this spec. Not a runtime dependency of the page. |
| A-S4 | Existing `requirements.md` (logo draft) | Adjacent artifact | Related brand thinking only. Not a blocker and not in-page Jira/logo delivery. |

No production backend, identity provider, or issue tracker is an actor for this page.

---

### 5. Functional requirements (numbered, testable)

- **FR-1:** The page shall set the browser document title to exactly `Hari-Agents`.
- **FR-2:** The page shall display a visible primary heading whose accessible name is `Hari-Agents`.
- **FR-3:** The page shall display a greeting that includes the word `Welcome` and the product name `Hari-Agents` (see **Assumption A-3** for the default sentence).
- **FR-4:** The page shall display a short branding line that states the surface is a personal agent workspace.
- **FR-5:** The page shall present FR-2, FR-3, and FR-4 in the first viewport of a typical desktop window without requiring a click, form submit, or network call to an application API.
- **FR-6:** The page shall be deliverable as static files and shall not require a backend process, database, or authenticated session to render the welcome content.
- **FR-7:** The page shall not collect input (no login form, search form, or required fields) in this release.
- **FR-8:** The page shall not embed analytics, tracking pixels, or third-party telemetry scripts.
- **FR-9:** The primary heading shall be a single `h1` (or equivalent semantic heading) so assistive technology can identify the page name.
- **FR-10:** Visible text on the default background shall remain readable (see **NFR-1**).
- **FR-11:** The same welcome content shall remain readable when the viewport is about 1280×800 and when it is about 375×667; horizontal overflow that clips the heading or greeting is not acceptable.
- **FR-12:** If a decorative mark is shown beside the name, the product name `Hari-Agents` shall remain visible as text so identity does not depend on an image load.

**Non-functional constraints (testable without a backend; not a tech-stack mandate)**

- **NFR-1:** Body and heading text shall meet WCAG 2.2 contrast of at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text against the chosen background.
- **NFR-2:** The page shall render its required content from local/static files when opened in a current Chromium-based desktop browser (see **Assumption A-5**).
- **NFR-3:** Technology stack, bundler, framework, and hosting product are **not requirements**. Those are architecture decisions, provided the delivered page meets FR-1 through FR-12 as a static welcome surface.

---

### 6. User stories

**US-1 — Recognize the workspace**

As a workspace owner,  
I want the landing page to be titled Hari-Agents,  
so that I can confirm I opened the correct personal agent workspace.

**US-2 — Feel welcomed**

As a visitor,  
I want to see a greeting on the welcome page,  
so that the first screen feels intentional rather than an empty folder or default browser page.

**US-3 — Understand the purpose**

As a visitor,  
I want a short branding line that this is a personal agent workspace,  
so that I understand the page’s purpose without reading other documents.

**US-4 — Use it without a server**

As an implementer,  
I want the welcome page to work as static files,  
so that I can verify it in a browser without standing up APIs, auth, or Jira.

**US-5 — Keep identity if imagery fails**

As a visitor,  
I want the name Hari-Agents to appear as text,  
so that I can still identify the workspace if a decorative image does not load.

---

### 7. Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then)

- **AC-FR-1.1:** Given the welcome page files are opened in a browser, when the page finishes loading, then the document title shown in the tab is `Hari-Agents`.
- **AC-FR-2.1:** Given the welcome page is visible, when a user views the main content, then a primary heading displaying `Hari-Agents` is on screen.
- **AC-FR-2.2:** Given the page DOM is inspected, when the main heading is queried, then there is exactly one `h1` whose text is `Hari-Agents`.
- **AC-FR-3.1:** Given the welcome page is visible, when a user reads the main content, then a greeting containing `Welcome` and `Hari-Agents` is visible without interaction.
- **AC-FR-4.1:** Given the welcome page is visible, when a user reads the main content, then supporting text identifies the surface as a personal agent workspace.
- **AC-FR-5.1:** Given a desktop viewport of about 1280×800, when the page loads, then the heading, greeting, and branding line are visible without scrolling away from the first screen and without submitting a form.
- **AC-FR-6.1:** Given no application server, API, or login session is running, when the static page is opened in the browser, then FR-2, FR-3, and FR-4 still render.
- **AC-FR-7.1:** Given the welcome page is loaded, when a user inspects the page, then there is no login, signup, or required input form.
- **AC-FR-8.1:** Given the welcome page source is reviewed, when scripts and network requests after load are checked in the browser, then no analytics or tracking endpoint is called.
- **AC-FR-10.1:** Given the default theme of the page, when contrast of heading and greeting text is checked against the background, then the ratios meet NFR-1.
- **AC-FR-11.1:** Given a viewport of about 375×667, when the page loads, then the heading and greeting remain fully readable and are not clipped by horizontal overflow.
- **AC-FR-12.1:** Given any decorative image is blocked or missing, when the page renders, then the text `Hari-Agents` remains visible and no broken-image icon is the only identifier.

All criteria above are verifiable by opening the static page and using browser UI, DevTools, or a contrast checker. No backend assertions are required.

---

### 8. Assumptions (explicitly labeled)

- **Assumption A-1:** “Hari-Agents” is the official product/workspace name for this page. No legal or trademark review has been provided.
- **Assumption A-2:** The page is a personal landing surface for a Cursor/agent workspace owned by the requester, not a multi-tenant product.
- **Assumption A-3:** Default greeting copy is: `Welcome to Hari-Agents`. A different greeting may replace this if the requester supplies one.
- **Assumption A-4:** Default branding line is: `A personal agent workspace.` This is placeholder copy, not approved marketing language.
- **Assumption A-5:** First verification target is a current desktop Chrome or Edge browser. Other browsers are desirable but not specified by the requester.
- **Assumption A-6:** English-only copy is sufficient for this release. No internationalization is required.
- **Assumption A-7:** Light, readable default styling is sufficient. Dark mode, theme toggle, and motion preferences are not requested.
- **Assumption A-8:** No approved logo artwork was supplied for this story. A text wordmark satisfies branding; creating a full logo system is not required to accept this page.
- **Assumption A-9:** The existing repo-root `requirements.md` (logo identity) remains a separate draft and does not change in-scope work for this welcome page.
- **Assumption A-10:** File name, folder, and whether the page lives at site root are architecture/implementation decisions, not business requirements, provided the delivered surface is the Hari-Agents welcome page.
- **Assumption A-11:** No deadline, environment, or release train was given.
- **Assumption A-12:** Downstream SDLC agents will consume this specification; this analysis does not implement the page or write Jira issues.

---

### 9. Dependencies and risks

**Dependencies**

- **D-1:** An implementer and a browser to open static files.
- **D-2:** Architecture decision on how the static page is produced and where it is placed in the workspace (not a functional requirement).
- **D-3:** Optional later reuse of logo assets from the separate logo draft, only if that work is approved and assets exist. **Not a blocker.**
- **D-4:** Requester confirmation of greeting/tagline if the assumed copy in A-3 and A-4 is unacceptable.

**Risks**

- **R-1:** Scope creep into a multi-page agent portal, chat UI, or Jira-connected dashboard. This spec intentionally stops at one static page.
- **R-2:** Treating stack choice (React, bundler, hosting) as a requirement could delay a page that only needs static markup.
- **R-3:** Relying on an image-only title would fail FR-12 if assets are missing.
- **R-4:** The workspace is a Cursor config git repo, not an application repo. Implementing files here without an architecture decision may mix product UI with editor configuration.
- **R-5:** The existing logo `requirements.md` could be mistaken for this welcome-page spec and pull favicon/PWA/OG work into v1.

---

### 10. Open questions

- **Q-1:** Is the assumed greeting `Welcome to Hari-Agents` and tagline `A personal agent workspace.` approved, or is different copy required?
- **Q-2:** Should implementation live in this Cursor config repo or in a separate application location? (Architecture decision; business need is only that the page exists and is verifiable.)
- **Q-3:** Is any decorative mark required besides the text wordmark, or is text-only branding acceptable for acceptance?
- **Q-4:** After this page, is a later multi-page workspace intended, or is a single welcome page the full requested product for now?
- **Q-5:** Is there a preferred visual direction (colors, density) beyond “clear, branded, readable”? None was specified.
- **Q-6:** Should this specification replace, sit beside, or remain separate from the existing logo `requirements.md`? **Recommendation:** keep them separate.

None of these questions blocks drafting or implementing the static page if A-3, A-4, and A-8 are accepted.

---

### 11. Recommended next steps

**Recommendation:** Treat this document as the approved-for-draft requirement input to the next SDLC stage. Do not create Jira issues unless the requester explicitly asks.

1. **Architecture (next):** Decide only what is needed for one static page (file location, whether plain HTML/CSS is enough, how it will be opened for test). Do not introduce a full application stack unless a later story needs it.
2. **Design:** Specify layout, typography, spacing, and color so FR-2–FR-5 and NFR-1 can be implemented without inventing brand rules at coding time. Keep a single screen.
3. **Implementation:** Build the static Hari-Agents welcome page and verify AC-FR-1.1 through AC-FR-12.1 in the browser with no backend.
4. **Test:** Execute the Given/When/Then criteria above as a short static-page checklist.
5. **Product confirmation:** Confirm or replace the assumed greeting and tagline (Q-1).
6. **Backlog hygiene:** Leave the logo draft as a separate item; do not fold favicon/PWA/OG or Jira-in-page work into this welcome page unless a new request says so.
